title: Phil Ponce brings Fats to Victor with a small band; $13 for the first date
summary: Manager Phil Ponce brought Fats from Cincinnati's WLW and talked a reluctant Victor into a six-piece band; the first date paid $13 each, the second a raise, then it took off.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well Herman, this recording session you did with Fats was the first one, you say, of a series that Fats did with this small group at Victor. How did this happen? Who was after who? Fats? Or Victor?

Well, here's what happened. A very good friend of ours, a man that was handling Fats then, Phil Ponce, and well, to me he was a great guy. To Fats he was a great guy. You see, in the meantime, Fats was in Cincinnati, working there by himself, and he start --
Was that when he was at WLW?

Yeah, WLW. Well Phil Ponce was there with him, in -- holding his arm up, you know. In other words, his ego, and trying to help him out, and telling him he should do this and do the other, and Phil was a good man for him, so if -- they came through that thing out there, and from there Phil brought him to New York.
Now, when they got to New York Victor -- he talked Victor into letting Fats have a small band, six-piece band, and they screamed Murder, never! You know, never heard --

Well, they'd never had a small group, a small band like that before, and they didn't think it would be advisable. They didn't think it would pay, and would be nice, and so and so and so and so. So they finally agreed, under some reason why I do not know, but I'm glad they did, because when we started recording, well, it was fair. (Laughs.) As our first date came to -- they paid us $13.00 for the first day.

(Laughs) I don't know what Fats got. But I know that's what I got, because the thing didn't do so well. Okay. So we took the thirteen bucks, and the next time we recorded we got a raise, $3.00, I think it was.
(Laughs.) Well how long did it take before they wanted Fats back to do another one?

No, that's what I'm saying now. The next date was Three bucks, and it -- the thing began to turn. It was a standstill. I mean nothing happened. Now, on the second date it -- the wheel began to turn a little bit. They said aw, well, there's a possibility. And from there we went into it and worked it up until we got into money, and after that -- after -- well, the world knows, he was the greatest recording artist ever.
And Victor still thinks he's the greatest. I know he was the greatest. But I -- that's the way it went, you know. But we were the first six-piece group that ever was, I mean --
